record.what_it_does: Financial data API linking bank accounts: transactions, balances, identity, payments, income.
record.auth_notes: The core API uses a team-level client_id and secret, sent in the request body or as PLAID-CLIENT-ID and PLAID-SECRET headers. Each end user connects a bank through Plaid Link, which produces a per-Item access_token used in later calls. OAuth (client_credentials grant via /oauth/token, scope mcp:dashboard) is documented only for the Dashboard MCP server. Plaid does not act as an OAuth provider that lets third-party apps act for Plaid customers. OAuth in Link refers to bank-side OAuth connections.
record.access_notes: Sandbox keys are self-serve on Dashboard signup. Live data needs Production access, which is requested in the Dashboard ("To view pricing, apply for Production access"). Plaid then notifies the team when Production is enabled. US/CA teams must also complete a risk and security questionnaire before accessing certain bank APIs, and OAuth institutions have registration requirements; Schwab can take up to 5 business days after approval. Plans: free Trial (10 Production Items, US/Canada teams created on or after 2026-04-15), Pay-as-you-go, Growth (annual minimum), and Custom/Scale. EU/UK customers can only use Custom plans.
record.api_breadth_notes: Products include Link, Auth, Transactions, Balance, Identity, Assets, Investments, Liabilities, Income, Transfer, Identity Verification, and others. This is well over 50 endpoints, but I did not count them exactly. A full OpenAPI spec is published in github.com/plaid/plaid-openapi.
record.mcp_notes: Dashboard MCP server: https://api.dashboard.plaid.com/mcp/ (Streamable HTTP, Bearer token from /oauth/token with the client_credentials grant and mcp:dashboard scope). It works with Production data only and requires Production approval. It covers Dashboard and diagnostic tasks, not end-user financial data. Plaid also offers a local MCP server in its AI coding toolkit, which provides mock data, docs search, Sandbox tokens, and webhook simulation.
record.blocker_notes: Sandbox is self-serve. Live bank data requires Production enablement by Plaid. Some bank APIs also need the security questionnaire and institution registration. Each end user must link accounts through Plaid Link. Credentials are per developer team, and there is no third-party OAuth, so a multi-tenant toolkit would need customers to supply their own client_id and secret plus Item access_tokens.
